title: News Feed: Caching, Pagination, and Real-time Updates
description: Add Redis caching, cursor-based pagination, and push-based feed updates.

data.text: Generating a feed for 1 billion users is expensive. Design caching, pagination, and real-time updates so the feed feels instant.
When a user creates a post, push it to all followers' pre-built feeds. Read is O(1) from cache. Write is O(followers).

data.title: Fan-out on Write with Redis

data.text: When a user requests their feed, fetch recent posts from all followed users on demand. Simpler but slower for users with many followings.

data.title: Push vs Pull Comparison
items: **Push (Fan-out on Write)**: Fast reads, expensive writes for celebrities with millions of followers.
**Pull (Fan-out on Read)**: Slow reads, simple writes. Better for users with few followings.
**Hybrid**: Push for normal users, pull for celebrity followers (inverted fan-out).
**Cache warming**: Pre-generate feeds during low-traffic hours.

data.title: The Celebrity Problem
data.text: A user with 50 million followers would trigger 50 million writes per post. The hybrid approach solves this: push to normal followers, and let celebrity followers pull the post when they load their feed.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Push model makes reads O(1) from Redis
Pull model is simpler but O(followings) per read
Hybrid balances write cost and read latency
Cursor-based pagination is more stable than offset-based
data.takeaway: Feed scalability is a caching and fan-out problem. Choose push, pull, or hybrid based on your average follower count distribution.
